persona: Dutch exchange student (Sanne de Vries) keeping her own fermentation batch log in a food-science lab, entering numbers the way she learned at home (comma decimal, dot thousands separator, dd.mm.yyyy dates) even though the lab's template is English-labeled
source_style: personal lab notebook kept in Excel, one row per fermentation batch over a month

columns.name: Date
columns.notes: European day.month.year format stored as text, e.g. '02.02.2026'; a naive US-locale date parser would misread day/month for the first 12 days

columns.name: Temperature_C
columns.notes: Real Excel number (General format), 20.0-28.0, one decimal. Normal control column with NO locale quirk, for contrast against the two required-quirk columns.

columns.name: Yield_Percent
columns.notes: REQUIRED QUIRK: stored as a real float fraction between 0.60 and 0.98 with cell.number_format == '0%', so e.g. stored value 0.63 displays as '63%'. Confirmed by read-back: all 31 cells have number_format '0%' and hold a float in [0,1], not the displayed percent integer.

columns.name: TotalSugar_mg_per_L
columns.notes: REQUIRED QUIRK: European-formatted numbers stored as TEXT strings (dot = thousands separator, comma = decimal separator). Row 2 = '1.234,5' (true value 1234.5), row 3 = '3,5' (true value 3.5). About 1 in 4 rows uses a value >=1000 mg/L (thousands-dot form), the rest are small values with a plain decimal comma.

columns.name: Notes
columns.notes: Free text, mostly empty (13 of 31 rows filled); values like 'sample lost', 'repeat run', 'diluted 1:10', 'contamination suspected'

clean_table.description: After cleaning: Yield_Percent already numeric (multiply by 100 only if you want a percent-scaled number rather than a proportion -- do NOT re-divide by 100, the stored value already IS the proportion). TotalSugar_mg_per_L must be re-parsed from European convention: strip '.' thousands separators, replace ',' with '.', then cast to float ('1.234,5' -> 1234.5, '3,5' -> 3.5). Date should be parsed as dd.mm.yyyy, not mm.dd.yyyy. 31 data rows, no missing BatchID/Substrate/Temperature/Yield/Sugar/Operator; Notes has 18 blanks.
clean_table.structure: One row per BatchID (B001..B031), no repeats or nesting.

intended_analysis: Compare fermentation yield (%) and total sugar concentration across substrates and operators; correlate temperature with yield.
mess_applied: Yield_Percent stored as a raw fraction (0-1) but DISPLAYED as a whole percent via a '%' cell number_format -- reading the underlying value without respecting the format silently gives a number 100x too small
TotalSugar_mg_per_L stored as TEXT in European number convention: '.' as thousands separator, ',' as decimal separator (e.g. '1.234,5' = 1234.5; '3,5' = 3.5)
Date column is text in dd.mm.yyyy order, ambiguous with mm.dd.yyyy for day values <=12
what_a_naive_reader_would_get_wrong: A tool that reads the raw Yield_Percent cell values without checking number_format would treat 0.63 as '63% yield' being stored as 0.63 -- fine if it knows to treat it as a proportion, but a naive summary that assumes percent columns are stored 0-100 would report yields around 0.7% instead of 70%. Separately, a naive numeric parser (or one that strips '.' as a thousands separator using US conventions) applied to TotalSugar_mg_per_L would parse '1.234,5' as 1.2345 (dropping 3 orders of magnitude) and would either fail to parse '3,5' at all or read it as '35' if the comma is stripped as if it were a thousands separator. The dd.mm.yyyy Date strings would also be silently misread as month/day for any day-of-month <=12.
